scenarios.prompt: port my app onto the template

expect.behavior: treats the incoming source as a read-only reference, never committed and never edited
produces an inventory that doubles as the parity contract the port must preserve
buckets every subsystem with a recorded why rather than an unexplained verdict
extracts the real design tokens rather than impressions of the design
expect.anchor: parity lives or dies on these

reject: edits or commits the original source into the new repo's history
buckets subsystems from a skim with no recorded comparison

scenarios.prompt: here's my existing site's source — it won't build locally

expect.behavior: records the reference grade honestly and lets it set the parity evidence per row
proceeds on inspection alone rather than blocking on a codebase that won't boot
expect.anchor: static-only is a grade, not a failure

expect.behavior: carries the original's green tests as portable characterization suites, not just signals

reject: blocks the adoption until the original runs locally
claims side-by-side parity evidence it cannot actually produce

scenarios.prompt: merge the boilerplate into my app

expect.behavior: says at intake that the mechanism is scaffold-plus-port, not an in-place merge
enumerates the incoming agent setup as an investment to disposition, not clutter
ships the union of both agentic layers, resolving collisions by the same bar

reject: silently drops the incoming skills, hooks, and instruction files
presents the disposition map without saying in plain language what stays theirs
